item.title: AfD surge in eastern Germany makes some immigrants question whether they still belong
item.description: Shahd Najeeb still remembers the trauma of fleeing Islamic State fighters during Syria's civil war. More than a decade after finding refuge in Germany, she now fears she may no longer be welcome there.
item.dc:creator: Amina Ismail, James Mackenzie
item.content:encoded: Shahd Najeeb still remembers the trauma of fleeing Islamic State fighters during Syria's civil war. More than a decade after finding refuge in Germany, she now fears she may no longer be welcome there. "When I think about the time we left Syria, I still don't know how we managed to get through it," she told Reuters in her home in Rostock, on Germany's Baltic coast. "It was like a nightmare." Najeeb and her husband, Mahmoud Hmouech, fled their home in Deir al-Zor in eastern Syria and rebuilt their lives in Germany, where he works in a barber shop and she serves meals in local schools. They have two young children. "We are grateful to the German people for welcoming us and giving us peace and security," Hmouech said. "The work we do is a small way of showing our gratitude." They are among more than 900,000 Syrians living in Germany, most of whom arrived as asylum seekers during the civil war. But as the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) gains support and migration returns to the centre of political debate, migrants say hostility towards foreigners is growing. Reuters spoke to 20 people of migrant background in Rostock and the nearby city of Schwerin, many of whom have become German citizens and have lived in Germany for years. Most said they had encountered more anti-immigrant abuse in recent years, ranging from muttered remarks to demands that they return to their countries of origin. One woman said a neighbour poured foul-smelling water on her from a balcony. Their concerns come as the AfD gains momentum across eastern Germany. In Najeeb and Hmouech's home state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, in the formerly communist east, opinion polls suggest the AfD is set to become the biggest party [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"in an election"] on Sunday. Earlier this month, the party, which wants to restrict immigration and talks about "remigration" - or sending foreigners back to their home countries - [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"won its first major regional election"] in Saxony-Anhalt, another eastern state. Several interviewees, including people working in healthcare, tourism, education and food services, said they would consider leaving Rostock or Schwerin if the climate continued to worsen. 'THIS COUNTRY IS FOR GERMANS' Sitting in the family's small apartment in northern Rostock, where their children's drawings cover one wall and toys are neatly stacked in corners of the living room, Najeeb spoke as her children, aged 6 and 4, played nearby. Najeeb, who studied physics in Baghdad and later worked as a jewellery designer in Syria, recalled stopping at a grocery store after collecting her children from school when, she said, an elderly man in a wheelchair shouted that she did not belong in Germany. "This country is for Germans," he yelled. "The pain I experienced in Rostock is a new kind of pain that I have never felt before," Najeeb said. "You feel the injustice because you have done nothing wrong. I worked hard to build a life for myself and then someone comes along and treats you like garbage," she said, her voice cracking. She recalled her son asking: "Mama, why is he insulting you? What did you do to him?" Unsure how to explain, she told him the man was perhaps unwell. LABOUR FORCE The AfD began as a eurosceptic party in 2013 and its anti-immigrant tone sharpened markedly after former Chancellor Angela Merkel's decision in 2015 to open Germany's borders temporarily, admitting around one million migrants and refugees, around a third of them Syrians fleeing the civil war. Since then, it has grown from a fringe movement into Germany's most popular party, leading Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives in national polls. Leif-Erik Holm, the AfD's main candidate in Sunday's election, says he has "absolutely no objection" to immigration by skilled workers. He says those who should be deported are the more than 250,000 foreigners who have no legal right to stay in Germany. But critics say the broader problem is the atmosphere created by rhetoric they say targets foreigners in general. During a televised debate on Wednesday, Social Democrat state premier Manuela Schwesig accused the AfD of "causing widespread fear with its statements on remigration and workers from different cultural backgrounds." "I think it's terrible that people who work here, who make their contribution and pay their taxes and social security contributions, are afraid and don't feel at ease," she said. During the debate, she and Holm took a question from a design engineer concerned at the risk of losing a valued Moroccan draughtsman because of the racist insults he said he encountered regularly on the street. Holm said it was "naturally a shame that there's such a mood". But he blamed the government for allowing illegal immigration and failing to deport more than a fraction of foreigners formally required to leave the country. The debate carries [USN:L8N44Z0LM TEXT:"economic implications"] as well. Around 50,000 people with a migration background work in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Economists have warned that like other eastern states with low birth rates and an ageing population, it will need more skilled workers. According to data from Germany's labour office, around 316,000 Syrian nationals - not including Syrians who have acquired German nationality - work in Germany, most in full-time jobs that pay social security contributions. Their unemployment rate is above 30%, but data show the longer people stay, the more likely they are to find work. Figures from 2023 indicate that among those who have been in Germany for seven years or longer, more than 60% have a job. Many Syrians say they hope to return home if conditions improve. Others, including Najeeb and Hmouech, increasingly see their future in Germany. Whether the AfD's rise changes that calculation remains an open question. Hmouech says he does not want his children to grow up feeling rejected by the society they call home. "At the end of the day, family comes first," he said.

item.title: WTA roundup: Defending champ Iva Jovic returns to Guadalajara final
item.description: Iva Jovic earned her lone career WTA Tour title last year at the Guadalajara Open. She is one win away from making it two straight at the same event.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iva Jovic earned her lone career WTA Tour title last year at the Guadalajara Open. She is one win away from making it two straight at the same event. The 18-year-old Los Angeles native, seeded second, rolled to a 6-4, 6-1 victory over sixth-seeded Cristina Bucsa of Spain in the semifinals on Friday in Mexico. Bucsa had plenty of opportunities in the match, but Jovic saved 11 of the 12 break points she faced. Jovic converted half of her eight break chances. Standing in the way of Jovic successfully defending her crown will be Peyton Stearns, who is pursuing her third career tournament victory. The 24-year-old Cincinnati native downed eighth-seeded Liudmila Samsonova of Russia 7-6 (7), 6-2 in the other semifinal. Stearns needed six set points to close the first set -- two with Samsonova serving at 5-6 and four more in the tiebreaker. In the second set, Stearns got an early break for a 2-1 edge and then pulled away. Stearns' tournament wins occurred at Rabat, Morocco, in May 2024 and at Austin, Texas, in February 2026. SP Open Mary Stoiana, a 23-year-old Texas A&M product, saw her best WTA Tour event come to an end when she lost 6-4, 6-2 to second-seeded Paula Badosa of Spain in a quarterfinal match at Sao Paulo. Badosa won 78% of her first-serve points while Stoiana managed just a 36% success rate on her first-serve points. The next opponent for Badosa will be Argentina's Nadia Podoroska, who edged the Netherlands' Suzan Lamens 7-6 (5), 3-6, 6-3. In the other semifinal, fourth-seeded Anna Blinkova of France will oppose seventh-seeded Kaitlin Quevedo of Spain. Quevedo eliminated Serbia's Teodora Kostovic 6-3, 6-4, and Blinkova knocked off eighth-seeded Alina Charaeva of Armenia 6-4, 7-5. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bravos logra primer triunfo en torneo mexicano de fútbol con doblete de colombiano Estupiñán
item.description: Bravos de Ciudad Juárez logró el viernes su primer triunfo en el torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano tras ganar por 2-0 a Tigres UANL con un doblete del colombiano Óscar Estupiñán en la novena jornada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bravos de Ciudad Juárez logró el viernes su primer triunfo en el torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano tras ganar por 2-0 a Tigres UANL con un doblete del colombiano Óscar Estupiñán en la novena jornada. A pesar de su primera victoria, Bravos, que registraba ocho derrotas consecutivas, se mantiene en el último lugar de la tabla general con tres puntos. En tanto, el club de la Universidad Autónoma de Nuevo León se estancó en el decimoquinto sitio con siete unidades. En el partido, disputado en el estadio Olímpico Benito Juárez, Bravos se puso en ventaja a los 66 minutos por la vía del tiro penal que anotó Estupiñán, después de que el centrocampista uruguayo Cesar Araújo cometió falta al panameño José Luis Rodríguez dentro del área. El segundo gol de Bravos cayó a los 79 minutos con el doblete de Estupiñán, quien remató con la cabeza un centro enviado por Rodríguez. En el otro partido del viernes, Puebla y Atlante empataron por 1-1 con goles del uruguayo Mathías Tomas y Walter Portales, respectivamente. El sábado se jugarán los encuentros entre Atlas-Pumas UNAM, Atlético de San Luis-Necaxa, Monterrey-Cruz Azul y América-Guadalajara. La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Pachuca enfrente a Tijuana, Toluca sea local ante Santos Laguna y León visite a Querétaro.

item.title: Mookie Betts belts 2 of Dodgers' 5 homers in rout of Giants
item.description: Mookie Betts homered twice, including his 53rd career leadoff homer, and Josue De Paula hit a tiebreaking double to help the Los Angeles Dodgers produce an 8-2 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Mookie Betts homered twice, including his 53rd career leadoff homer, and Josue De Paula hit a tiebreaking double to help the Los Angeles Dodgers produce an 8-2 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Friday night. Betts also hit one of Los Angeles' four eighth-inning homers as the Dodgers socked five overall while winning for the 12th time in the 15 games. Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker hit back-to-back homers in the eighth, and Betts and Will Smith repeated the feat later in the frame. Tyler Glasnow struck out a season-high 10 in six innings for Los Angeles (94-60), which trails the Milwaukee Brewers (96-58) by two games in the battle for the major leagues' best record. Betts is tied with Hall of Famer Craig Biggio for the fourth-most leadoff homers all-time and is one behind third-place Alfonso Soriano. Betts has hit 33 for the Dodgers after producing 20 for the Boston Red Sox. Hall of Famer Rickey Henderson tops the list with 81, and George Springer is second with 65. Glasnow (5-1) gave up two runs, three hits and two walks. He is 7-1 in 10 career appearances (nine starts) against San Francisco. Jung Hoo Lee homered and Jonah Cox had an RBI single as the Giants (64-90) fell for the fifth time in seven games. With the score 2-2, Tucker walked to start the bottom of the sixth before Jason Foley (3-2) retired the next two batters. De Paula then laced a double into the right-center-field gap to put the Dodgers in front. Los Angeles later played Home Run Derby off Giants left-hander Philip Abner in the eighth. Muncy hit the third pitch of the inning over the wall in right-center. Two pitches later, Tucker also cleared the right-center fence to give Los Angeles a three-run lead. Two outs later, De Paula walked before Betts homered to left-center, making it 7-2. Smith hit the second pitch in his at-bat over the wall in center. Cesar Perdomo started for the Giants and gave up two runs and six hits over 4 2/3 innings. He walked three and struck out one. Betts hit Perdomo's second pitch of the game over the fence in left-center to get the Dodgers started. The Giants tied it in the second when Lee slammed a 2-2 pitch over the wall in right. San Francisco moved ahead in the third as Scott Bandura singled and stole second to start the inning. There were two on and two outs later in the inning when Cox hit an RBI single to left. In the fifth, De Paula and Betts singled to start the inning. One out later, Teoscar Hernandez delivered a single to right to tie it at 2. --Field Level Media

item.title: Inside China's AI race
item.description: What does the AI race look like from inside China?
item.content:encoded: Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app. As the US and China race to dominate artificial intelligence, Reuters correspondents Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen say the two countries aren't even playing the same game. On this episode of On Assignment, they take us inside China's AI industry - from Beijing's push to weave AI into every corner of society, to the murky world of chip access, distillation and export controls. Hear what it takes to report on one of the most fast-moving industries on Earth, and why the answer to "who's winning" may depend entirely on how you define the race. item.title: Asian Olympic boss says politicians need to stay out of sport at Nagoya Games
item.description: Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani said on Saturday that politicians should not be involved in sports, following a diplomatic incident involving a Taiwan government official at the Asian Games.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani said on Saturday that politicians should not be involved in sports, following a diplomatic incident involving a Taiwan government official at the Asian Games. Taiwan sport minister Lee Yang, a former Olympic badminton champion, was initially blocked from attending a flag-raising ceremony at the Games on Friday, triggering a standoff as the Taiwan delegation refused to participate in protest. Lee was eventually permitted entry, with the ceremony taking place more than an hour after scheduled. Taiwan's cabinet complained Lee had been subject to "unreasonable obstruction" in a statement and that he had obtained the required access credentials. Sheikh Joaan said at a press conference he was unaware of the incident but that politicians needed to stay out of sports at the quadrennial Games. "I think that our focus here is on the athletes and on making sure that everyone, all the athletes, have the equal rights in competing and in having their freedom," the Qatari told reporters in Nagoya. "So I don't think the politicians or politics should be involved in sports. That's my opinion." OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam added that the flag-raising ceremony was meant for the participants in the Games. "(It's) not for the delegation from the ministry or from the government," he said. Lee claimed back-to-back badminton gold medals in the men's doubles at the Tokyo and Paris Olympics. The buildup to the Aichi-Nagoya Games has been overshadowed by complaints from national team delegations over organisational issues, including transport and the accommodations provided for athletes. Sheikh Joaan defended the local organisers saying they had been solving accommodation issues as they arise. "I think everything is hopefully being back on track," he said. The organisational problems have underscored the massive size of the Games, which include a record 43 sports and 469 medal events, dwarfing the summer Olympics' 32 sports and 329 events. The OCA defended the size of the programme at Nagoya, which will see the debut of "virtual" taekwondo while retaining breaking (breakdancing) and esports. "We are very proud that the Asian Games (are) bigger than any other games with low cost," said Al-Musallam.

item.title: Yankees score 5 runs in first inning to take down D-backs
item.description: Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr. homered and the New York Yankees scored five runs in the first inning to cruise to a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday in Phoenix.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr. homered and the New York Yankees scored five runs in the first inning to cruise to a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday in Phoenix. Lombard had two hits and three RBIs, and his two-run single capped the early five-run outburst against Eduardo Rodriguez (15-7), who walked three of the first four he faced. Rice tripled and walked twice as the Yankees played without Aaron Judge, who will be placed on the injured list Saturday, retroactive to Thursday, with a right calf strain. Gerrit Cole (9-9) gave up two runs on four hits in six innings. He struck out six, did not issue a walk, and retired 13 of the final 15 he faced after Corbin Carroll's two-run homer in the second made it 5-2. Carroll added a double and Geraldo Perdomo and Nolan Arenado had two hits apiece for the D-backs, who have lost five of six as their NL wild-card chances fade. The D-backs (80-74) are five games behind San Diego, Philadelphia and the Chicago Cubs (all 85-69) for the three NL wild-card spots. The Padres were the only one of the four to win Friday. The Yankees (89-64) have won four of five and eight of 10. The Yankees trail Tampa Bay by four games in the AL East, and the teams will meet in a four-game series in Yankee Stadium starting Tuesday. They are 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston for the first AL wild-card spot. Rodriguez, on pace to post a career-low ERA, gave up five hits and seven runs in 5 1/3 innings, leaving after Lombard's homer made it 7-2 in the sixth. He struck out five and walked four. The Yankees forced Rodriguez to use 45 pitches in their big first. Paul Goldschmidt walked to open the game and took third on Cody Bellinger's single before Heliot Ramos and Rice walked on 3-2 counts to force in the first run. Amed Rosario followed with an RBI single and Ramos scored on a wild pitch before Lombard capped the inning with a two-run single. Rice homered to lead off the third, Lombard homered in the sixth, and the Yankees turned an infield single and two Arizona errors into a two-run seventh to close the scoring. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bolivia scraps diesel subsidy to combat fuel shortages
item.description: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz on Friday announced the end of state diesel subsidies, shifting the country to a unified pricing model to help resolve chronic fuel shortages.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz on Friday announced the end of state diesel subsidies, shifting the country to a unified pricing model to help resolve chronic fuel shortages. Bolivia imports roughly 90% of its diesel, and the government spends approximately $55 million weekly on subsidies, according to Paz. "Starting today, diesel will cost what it costs us to buy abroad," Paz said, citing rampant fuel smuggling and black-market reselling as key drivers of the weekly deficit. The move replaces a dual-pricing system introduced in August that charged high-volume consumers 18 bolivianos ($2.60) per liter, while maintaining a subsidized rate of 9.80 bolivianos for others. Paz said domestic prices will now track global benchmarks, dropping if international costs decline. To offset the financial strain on households and key economic sectors, the administration unveiled targeted relief measures, including direct cash transfers and preferential credit lines.

item.title: Padres blast Marlins to draw even in wild-card race
item.description: Ty France clouted a three-run homer to cap a six-run fifth inning Friday night as the San Diego Padres stopped the visiting Miami Marlins 8-2 to forge a three-way tie atop the National League's wild-card standings.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ty France clouted a three-run homer to cap a six-run fifth inning Friday night as the San Diego Padres stopped the visiting Miami Marlins 8-2 to forge a three-way tie atop the National League's wild-card standings. Winning for the 11th time in 12 games, San Diego (85-69) pulled even with the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia, who both lost earlier Friday night. The Padres' magic number for clinching a playoff spot dropped to five. Nick Pivetta (3-2) earned the win by working the first five innings, yielding four hits and a run with a walk and four strikeouts. Marlins reliever Cade Gibson (5-2) was tagged with the loss after yielding the first two runs in the game-changing fifth. Xander Bogaerts led off with a double and reached third on Jake Cronenworth's single. Samad Taylor greeted reliever Tyler Zuber with a bunt single to fill the bases. After Ethan Salas' shallow fly ball netted Zuber an out, Fernando Tatis Jr. tied the game with an RBI single to right. Dustin Harris put San Diego ahead to stay with a two-run single up the middle. After Manny Machado lined out, France jacked a hanging sweeper an estimated 388 feet to left for his 21st homer, a career high. All that happened after Miami starter Tyler Phillips worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings, permitting only two hits and a walk while fanning three. He left with Miami holding a 1-0 edge after Agustin Ramirez lined a one-out homer to left in the third, his fifth. The Marlins' other run came in the eighth via a two-out RBI single by Javier Sanoja that scored Otto Lopez, who doubled to left with one out. Ramirez collected three of their 10 hits, while Sanoja and Lopez had two each. San Diego tacked on two more runs in its half of the eighth. Jackson Merrill led off by ripping his 26th homer of the year an estimated 432 feet to right. Three more singles, the last by Taylor, brought in Bogaerts. Harris, France, Bogaerts, Cronenworth and Taylor each bagged two of the Padres' 12 hits. --Field Level Media

item.title: New Zealand's Ravindra a doubt for India series after injury in promotional shoot
item.description: New Zealand all-rounder Rachin Ravindra dislocated his shoulder while filming a diving catch during a promotional shoot, making him a doubt for next month's Twenty20 series against India, the country's cricket board said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand all-rounder Rachin Ravindra dislocated his shoulder while filming a diving catch during a promotional shoot, making him a doubt for next month's Twenty20 series against India, the country's cricket board said on Saturday. The injury to Ravindra's right shoulder occurred in Auckland during a commercial shoot with Sky on Wednesday, New Zealand Cricket said in a statement. "Initial assessments by medical specialists ... have cleared major structural damage, but Ravindra’s return to play timeline will be determined by his progress during the first weeks of his rehabilitation," it said. Ravindra, 26, has represented New Zealand in 115 matches across all formats as a versatile batter who can slot into the top or middle order, and a left-arm finger-spinner. He was New Zealand's highest run-scorer in the 50-over World Cup in 2023 and their highest wicket-taker in this year's T20 World Cup, where they reached the final. "We are gutted for Rachin," said New Zealand's performance manager Mike Sandle. "As with all commercial shoots involving our players, the activities were agreed in advance by all parties, with appropriate safety measures in place. It was a bit of a freak accident, and we’ll continue to review our processes around events like this in the future." New Zealand will host India in five T20 matches from October 22, followed by five One-Day Internationals and two tests the following month.

item.title: Reports: Pistons, Ausar Thompson agree to five-year, $155 million extension
item.description: The Detroit Pistons and forward Ausar Thompson agreed to a five-year, $155 million extension on Friday, according to multiple media reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Pistons and forward Ausar Thompson agreed to a five-year, $155 million extension on Friday, according to multiple media reports. The fully guaranteed deal will begin with the 2027-28 season, according to The Athletic. Thompson was entering the final season of the rookie contract he signed after Detroit selected him fifth overall in the 2023 NBA draft. Still just 23 years old, Thompson is already widely regarded as one of the league's top defenders. He earned NBA All-Defensive first-team honors last season, becoming the first Pistons player to do so since Ben Wallace in 2005-06. Thompson also finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting, behind winner Victor Wembanyama and runner-up Chet Holmgren. In 73 games during the 2025-26 regular season, Thompson averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2 steals and 0.9 blocks. He added 8.2 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.8 blocks per game during Detroit's 14-game run to the Eastern Conference semifinals. In doing so, he became the first player since Anthony Davis in 2020 to record at least 25 steals and 25 blocks in a single postseason. Thompson and his twin, Houston Rockets forward Amen Thompson, are the first brothers in NBA history to each sign contracts worth at least $100 million. --Field Level Media

item.title: Mets 1B Jared Young (concussion) out for season
item.description: New York Mets first baseman Jared Young was home recovering from a concussion on Friday, and the team shut him down for the remainder of the season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Mets first baseman Jared Young was home recovering from a concussion on Friday, and the team shut him down for the remainder of the season. Young was knocked unconscious briefly after an on-field collision with teammate Nolan McLean on Thursday in the 3-0 loss to the visiting Philadelphia Phillies. He was taken off the field on a stretcher and transported to a hospital. A day later, he was still dealing with short-term memory issues and headaches, Mets interim manager Andy Green said. Green added that Young was doing "as good as could be expected and hoped for, given what we saw (Thursday) night. ... Everything we have heard has been really optimistic from a recovery standpoint, from a getting-back-on-the-field-eventually standpoint. I am relieved. I think everybody is." Regarding Young's long-term prognosis, Green said, "Very optimistic about recovery and continuing to play going forward. There's no concerns in that space." Young got hurt in the sixth inning on Thursday. McLean, the Mets' starting pitcher, moved toward first base to cover the bag on a dribbler hit by Justin Crawford. McLean was attempting to step over a nearly prone Young when he kneed Young in the head. Young was down on the field for a long time before being loaded on a stretcher. He gave a thumbs-up to the crowd as he was carted off the field. Crawford was safe on an infield single. McLean stayed in the game and struck out the next batter to end the inning, the last batter he faced. The Mets placed him on the seven-day injured list on Friday and recalled Ronny Mauricio from Triple-A Syracuse. Young, after going 0-for-2 on Thursday, finished the season with a .266 average, nine homers and 39 RBIs in 103 games. Young, 31, began his major league career with the Chicago Cubs in 2022 and '23, then joined the Mets ahead of the 2025 season. In 147 career games, he has a .249 career average with 15 homers and 53 RBIs. Mauricio, 25, hit .180 with one homer and two RBIs in 17 games for New York earlier this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Defence firm Anduril says US delay on Taiwan arms sales affecting its business
item.description: US defence tech firm Anduril's founder Palmer Luckey said on Saturday that President Donald Trump's delay in approving arms sales to Taiwan is affecting its business and that he has discussed this with Trump.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: US defence tech firm Anduril's founder Palmer Luckey said on Saturday that President Donald Trump's delay in approving arms sales to Taiwan is affecting its business and that he has discussed this with Trump. The $14 billion package for Taiwan has been awaiting Trump's approval for months. After a May summit in Beijing with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Trump said he was holding it in abeyance and described it as a "very good negotiating chip". China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own, an assertion Taipei rejects. The issue of Taiwan is likely to be high on Xi's agenda when he meets Trump in Washington next week. Speaking to reporters in Taipei where he attended a defence forum with Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, Luckey said he did not know the status of the arms package. "It's definitely affecting the business in that our business with Taiwan would be in a different place if you had that $14 billion moving forward," he said, declining to give details about what was being delayed for the company. DRONES RESHAPE WARFARE Anduril, whose Altius drone is used by Taiwan, has become one of Silicon Valley's hottest defence bets as drones reshape warfare in Ukraine and the Middle East and Trump pushes the Pentagon to adopt cutting-edge technologies to counter China. Luckey, whom [USN:L1N3XW05A TEXT:"China sanctioned"] in December for selling weapons to Taiwan, said one of the problems in delaying the package was that it had a broader, longer-lasting impact. "It's that as long as that's stuck, you don't have continued forward progress in other areas," he said. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside office hours. China has repeatedly told the US to stop selling weapons to Taiwan and has sanctioned numerous US companies that sell arms to the island. The US is bound by law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, though Trump has called that commitment into question. Luckey said he had discussed the issue of Taiwan arms sales with Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. He said the administration was open to hearing from people on the issue but aware of the fallout that could come from selling more weapons to Taiwan, such as China using its leverage with rare earths crucial for tech companies. "And so I've heard people say, shouldn't he just approve the deal and damn the consequences? But he's getting briefed by other people who are not me, and they're saying, 'If you do this, here's what's going to happen to American consumers'," Luckey said. "He has to weigh all of those things. He's in a really difficult, difficult situation," Luckey added, referring to Trump. Lai, who shook hands with Luckey at the forum's start, has made drones a central part of Taiwan's military modernisation. Last year, Taiwan unveiled its first missile to be jointly made with a US company, Anduril's [USN:L3N3V40PU TEXT:"Barracuda-500,"] an autonomous, low-cost cruise missile.

item.title: Connor Prielipp fires 7 strong innings as Twins blank Angels
item.description: Connor Prielipp allowed two hits over a career-high seven innings and fellow rookie Walker Jenkins went 3-for-4 with a home run as the Minnesota Twins registered a 3-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Friday in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Connor Prielipp allowed two hits over a career-high seven innings and fellow rookie Walker Jenkins went 3-for-4 with a home run as the Minnesota Twins registered a 3-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Friday in Anaheim, Calif. Prielipp (6-7) walked two and struck out eight. He left after throwing 92 pitches, 60 for strikes. Travis Adams pitched a 1-2-3 ninth inning to pick up his third save. Jenkins, who began his career going 4-for-45, homered for the second straight game on his sixth consecutive hit in the series. Brooks Lee added two hits and a run for Minnesota (72-82), which evened the four-game series at one win apiece. Jose Siri had two hits for Los Angeles (59-95). Grayson Rodriguez (4-8) gave up three runs on eight hits with no walks in 6 2/3 innings. He struck out four and threw 91 pitches, with 66 going for strikes. Minnesota jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the first inning. Luke Keaschall was hit by a pitch to start the game and advanced to third on a single by Lee. Kody Clemens then hit into a fielder's choice with Keaschall getting thrown at home following a lengthy rundown that allowed Lee and Clemens to advance to second and third. Ryan Jeffers followed with a sacrifice fly to drive in Lee, and Josh Bell drove in Clemens with a single to center. Los Angeles nearly cut the lead in half in the sixth inning when Zach Neto led off with a long drive to left, but Emmanuel Rodriguez jumped up at the fence to rob him of a home run. Jenkins then made it 3-0 in the seventh when he lined his third home run 357 feet off the foul pole netting in right. The Angels loaded the bases with no outs against reliever Tommy Nance in the eighth on back-to-back singles by Christian Moore, snapping an 0-for-21 drought, and Wade Meckler and a walk to Neto. But Nance got out of the jam with consecutive strikeouts of Mike Trout and pinch hitter Josh Lowe followed by a lineout to left by Vaughn Grissom. --Field Level Media

item.title: Death toll at 31 in Pakistan police compound attack, AFP reports

item.title: Kit blunder forces India to change Asian Games flagbearer
item.description: India have replaced their male flagbearer in Saturday's Asian Games opening ceremony in Nagoya, Japan, because the original choice, Tajinderpal Singh Toor, has not received his official ceremonial kit and cannot attend the event, media reports said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India have replaced their male flagbearer in Saturday's Asian Games opening ceremony in Nagoya, Japan, because the original choice, Tajinderpal Singh Toor, has not received his official ceremonial kit and cannot attend the event, media reports said. Toor, who is aiming for his third straight Asian Games gold in shot put, will be replaced by kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat as the male flagbearer. Shooter Manu Bhaker, who won two bronze medals at the Paris Olympics, is the female flagbearer. “I'm told that my kit will reach at 3 p.m. at the airport. Reaching the opening ceremony venue after collecting my kit from airport on time will be very difficult. So, I've told IOA (Indian Olympic Association) that I'm not coming for opening ceremony,” news agency PTI quoted Toor as saying. "My kit is lying in India ... IOA told me yesterday about me becoming flagbearer. Otherwise my coach, who reached here yesterday, could've picked it up for me." The IOA said in a statement that 31-year-old Toor would not be able to be India's flagbearer "due to a technical issue".

item.title: Sal Frelick's 10th-inning RBI sends Brewers past Orioles
item.description: Sal Frelick singled home a 10th-inning run and the visiting Milwaukee Brewers pulled out a 6-5 victory against the Baltimore Orioles on Friday in the opener of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Sal Frelick singled home a 10th-inning run and the visiting Milwaukee Brewers pulled out a 6-5 victory against the Baltimore Orioles on Friday in the opener of a three-game series. There was late-inning drama for both teams before Chad Patrick retired the Orioles in order in the bottom of the 10th for his sixth save. Trevor Megill (3-3) was the winning pitcher despite a blown save. Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio and Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit three-run homers early in the game, and then there were five consecutive innings with no scoring. With the score 3-3, the Brewers (96-58) took the lead with two runs in the top of the ninth. William Contreras delivered a run-scoring double off reliever Rico Garcia, and Christian Yelich hit a two-out RBI single against Grant Wolfram (6-4). The bottom of the ninth began with Gunnar Henderson's single and Coby Mayo's double off Megill. Samuel Basallo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand each followed with a sacrifice fly to even the score at 5-5. Chourio and Brice Turang both finished with two hits for the National League Central champion Brewers, who totaled 10 hits while winning for the eighth time in 10 games. Henderson and Mayo both collected three hits for the Orioles (75-79). Colton Cowser added two hits to Baltimore's 12-hit attack. The Orioles left 12 runners on base as their three-game winning streak ended and they endured a damaging loss in their quest for an American League wild card. Baltimore trails the Chicago White Sox (78-76) by three games for the last wild-card slot with eight games to go. Neither starting pitcher lasted long. Cade Povich worked 3 2/3 innings for Baltimore, surrendering three runs on five hits with two walks and three strikeouts. Dustin May of the Brewers logged 2 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on six hits and one walk with four strikeouts. Alonso socked his 38th homer of the season and his fifth in nine games. His RBI total rose to 105. The Brewers threatened in the eighth with three walks, but they stranded the bases loaded on Cooper Pratt's flyout. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers beat Blue Jays, gain ground in playoff race
item.description: Corey Seager capped a four-run second inning with an RBI double as the Texas Rangers opened a three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays with a 7-1 win on Friday in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Corey Seager capped a four-run second inning with an RBI double as the Texas Rangers opened a three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays with a 7-1 win on Friday in Arlington, Texas. Texas (77-77) drew 10 walks and moved into a first-place tie with the Houston Astros in the American League West. Toronto (76-78) fell one game behind the Rangers and two games back of the Chicago White Sox (78-76) for the final AL Wild Card spot. Jake Burger had two RBIs for the Rangers, who won for the fifth time in their last six games. Trevor Williams (2-0) closed the game by striking out four batters over four scoreless innings for the win. Myles Straw had two hits with an RBI for the Blue Jays, who committed three errors and lost for the third time in their last four games. Texas took a 4-0 lead in the second inning against Dylan Cease (11-6), who issued back-to-back walks before Lopez singled to load the bases. With one out, shortstop Ernie Clement made a throwing error on Evan Carter fielder's choice grounder, allowing two runs to score. Another run scored on Ezequiel Duran's sacrifice fly before Seager capped the rally with an RBI double to right field. Cease allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits over 2 2/3 innings. He walked six and struck out three. Toronto got on the board against Kumar Rocker in the fifth inning when Josh Smith scored from second on Straw's one-out double. Rocker gave up one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over 4 1/3 innings. The Rangers added to their lead with a run in the fifth when Brandon Nimmo scored on Burger's sacrifice fly. Toronto's control issues surfaced again with one out in the sixth inning, when Langford drew a bases-loaded walk from Brendon Little. The Blue Jays escaped further damage when Jose Rodriguez replaced Little for his major league debut and recorded two quick outs. Texas tacked on a run in the eighth inning on Burger's RBI double against Joe Mantiply. --Field Level Media

item.title: US fashion council CEO Kolb resigns after clash with runway show protesters
item.description: Steven Kolb resigned as head of the Council of Fashion Designers of America on Friday, days after coming under fire for physically restraining animal rights activists at a New York Fashion Week runway show.
item.dc:creator: Ruchika Khanna
item.content:encoded: Steven Kolb resigned as head of the Council of Fashion Designers of America on Friday, days after coming under fire for physically restraining animal rights activists at a New York Fashion Week runway show. "After twenty years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and President," Kolb said in a post on his Substack. The CFDA, the leading US fashion-industry trade group and organizer of New York Fashion Week, said on Tuesday that Kolb was on leave pending a full review by the council's board, after he said he was taking a voluntary leave. On Sunday, Kolb [USN:L6N4570YE TEXT:"grabbed at least two activists"] protesting H&M-owned COS's (HMb.ST) use of wool during a runway show. He pinned one protester to the ground and covered her mouth with his hand, according to videos viewed by Reuters that circulated widely online. Kolb apologized on Monday, saying he planned to meet with People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, which had organized the protest. "There is no justification for physically restraining another person," he said at the time. "Security should have handled the situation, and I should have stepped back." Kolb's physical confrontation with the activists led to a widespread backlash, with PETA on Sunday saying his actions "show how top people in fashion use violence to silence people" advocating for animal rights. The CFDA board, led by Thom Browne and including designers such as Vera Wang, Ralph Lauren and Michael Kors, said in an Instagram post that it respected Kolb's decision to step down and thanked him for his years of service. The CFDA did not name a successor.

item.title: Lazaro Montes’ 9th-inning homer lifts Mariners past Rockies
item.description: Lazaro Montes homered leading off the top of the ninth, J.P. Crawford also went deep and the Seattle Mariners beat the host Colorado Rockies 5-4 in Denver on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lazaro Montes homered leading off the top of the ninth, J.P. Crawford also went deep and the Seattle Mariners beat the host Colorado Rockies 5-4 in Denver on Friday night. Randy Arozarena finished with three hits, Carlos Vargas (2-0) recorded one out for the win for Seattle (72-82) and Andres Munoz earned his 28th save. With the game tied 4-all, Montes launched a 426-foot homer into the second deck in right field off Jordan Romano (0-4). Cole Carrigg led off the bottom of the ninth with a single and stole second but was caught stealing third. Munoz then fanned Mickey Moniak to end the game. Carrigg, Connor Norby and Jake McCarthy had three hits apiece and Ezequiel Tovar contributed two hits for Colorado (56-98). Down 3-2, the Rockies rallied in the sixth. Tovar reached on a one-out single, chasing starter Bryan Woo, and then stole second against reliever Gabriel Speier. McCarthy tripled to center to tie it and scored on Norby's single to give Colorado the lead. Seattle tied it in the seventh when Michael Arroyo, who led off with a double, scored on Dominic Canzone's sacrifice fly. Woo allowed three runs on 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings. The Mariners jumped on Colorado starter Gabriel Hughes in the first inning. Crawford hit his 18th career leadoff homer to open the night and Arozarena and Canzone hit consecutive doubles to put runners on second and third. Hughes struck out the next two before Josh Naylor ripped a single to right to drive in two runs. The rookie right-hander settled down after that single, retiring 11 in a row until a one-out walk to Brock Rodden in the fifth. He left after Arozarena's two-out infield single. Hughes allowed three runs on five hits and fanned six in 4 2/3 innings. The Rockies answered with a run in the bottom of the first on Carrigg's RBI single but squandered a leadoff triple from Moniak in the second. They scored again with two outs in the fourth when Tovar doubled and came home on McCarthy's single. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tigers wipe out 6-run deficit, knock White Sox out of first place
item.description: Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as the visiting Detroit Tigers stormed back from six runs down to beat the Chicago White Sox 11-8 on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as the visiting Detroit Tigers stormed back from six runs down to beat the Chicago White Sox 11-8 on Friday. The loss dropped Chicago (78-76) one game behind Cleveland (79-75) in the American League Central after the Guardians beat the Athletics 5-3 on Friday. Detroit trailed 8-2 before scoring nine unanswered runs, capped by the eighth-inning explosion. Hao-Yu Lee tied the game with a two-run homer off Sean Newcomb (2-5). Three batters later, Dingler singled to right off Bryan Hudson to put the Tigers ahead. Greene followed with a blast to right field. Lee went 4-for-5 with three RBIs and two runs, and teammate Kevin McGonigle finished 2-for-5 with four RBIs. The White Sox jumped on Tigers starter Andrew Sears for six runs in the first after Detroit struck for a run in the top of the inning. Chicago loaded the bases with two walks and an error before a wild pitch scored Tommy Pham. An error by Lee at third base brought home another run before Colson Montgomery ripped a three-run double to right field for a 5-1 lead. Sears was replaced by Beau Brieske, and Miguel Vargas followed with an RBI double. After McGonigle hit an RBI single in the top of the third, Vargas crushed his 32nd home run, a two-run shot in bottom of the third that pushed the lead to 8-2. The Tigers (73-81) started chipping away in the fifth. McGonigle ripped a bases-clearing triple to deep right-center field to make it 8-5 before Lee's RBI double in the sixth pulled Detroit within two. Sears lasted just two-thirds of an inning, allowing one hit and six runs, none earned, while walking three. White Sox starter David Sandlin gave up five runs on seven hits over four-plus innings, walking one and striking out four. Tigers reliever Drew Sommers (2-4) struck out five in two scoreless, hitless innings. Kenley Jansen worked a 1-2-3 ninth for his 21st save. --Field Level Media

item.title: China investigates Meituan and Alibaba units for suspected antitrust violations
item.description: China's market regulator is investigating Meituan unit Beijing Sankuai Information Technology for suspected violations of unfair competition laws, the country's official CCTV broadcaster reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's market regulator is investigating Meituan (3690.HK) unit Beijing Sankuai Information Technology for suspected violations of unfair competition laws, the country's official CCTV broadcaster reported on Saturday. China has been cracking down on monopolistic behaviour, most recently fining Trip.com (9961.HK) [USN:L1N43R00Q TEXT:"5.2 billion yuan"] ($776.41 million) over what the regulator said was its online hotel-booking monopoly, as Beijing struggles to bolster consumption amid a slowing economy. The Beijing branch of the State Administration for Market Regulation said Alibaba (9988.HK) unit Hangzhou Taomei Aviation Services, Tongcheng Network Technology and Tujia Online Information Technology (Tianjin) were also subject to investigation after preliminary findings, according to CCTV. Tongcheng and Tujia said in posts on their official WeChat accounts that their operations are normal and that they are cooperating with authorities. Meituan said in a post on its official website that it will cooperate with authorities. Hangzhou Taomei said in an official WeChat post it is cooperating with regulators. The China Hotel Association said on Saturday that Beijing's branch of SAMR has started investigating four online hotel and travel booking platforms for unfair competitive practices, without identifying the operators of the platforms. The statement on the association's website said the move followed a meeting held by the SAMR and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism for the online booking industry. ($1 = 6.6975 Chinese yuan)

item.title: Cade Cavalli reaches 200 strikeouts as Nationals rout Cardinals
item.description: Cade Cavalli pitched five scoreless innings and recorded the 200th strikeout of his first full major league season Friday night, leading the Washington Nationals to a 9-1 victory against the host St. Louis Cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cade Cavalli pitched five scoreless innings and recorded the 200th strikeout of his first full major league season Friday night, leading the Washington Nationals to a 9-1 victory against the host St. Louis Cardinals. Cavalli, who agreed to a four-year contract extension with the Nationals earlier in the day that could be worth up to $70 million, allowed four hits and struck out six. He is the seventh pitcher with at least 200 strikeouts so far this season. With his ace staked to a big lead thanks in part to a two-run home run by Dylan Crews and a two-run double by Yohandy Morales, manager Blake Butera pulled Cavalli after he threw 73 pitches. Cavalli (13-5) earned strikeout No. 200 on the final pitch of his outing, a changeup on the inside corner that froze JJ Wetherholt without a swing to end the fifth. Cavalli gave a smile and pumped his fist as he walked off the field with catcher Harry Ford. He has posted a 1.90 ERA in 12 second-half starts. Cavalli is the first Nats pitcher to reach 200 strikeouts in a season since Patrick Corbin, Max Scherzer and Stephen Strasburg did it in the 2019 World Series season. Cavalli's extension guarantees him $47 million and could be worth up to $70 million if the Nationals exercise their 2031 team option. The Nationals (72-82) pushed three runs across in the first inning, keyed by an RBI single from CJ Abrams and a run-scoring fielder's choice grounder from Brady House. Abrams also stole second base in the first to become the first Nats player since Alfonso Soriano in 2006 to reach 30 homers and 30 steals in the same season. Crews' 12th homer of the year came during a four-run third against Kyle Leahy (10-5). Leahy allowed seven runs -- six earned -- along with five hits and three walks over three innings. Brad Lord followed Cavalli with two scoreless frames, and the Cardinals (75-79) scored their lone run against right-hander Jack Sinclair in the eighth on an RBI grounder by Ivan Herrera. Josiah Gray pitched a one-hit ninth for Washington, which has won five of six. --Field Level Media

item.title: Famed Inter Milan and Italy forward Mazzola dies at 83
item.description: Former Italy forward Sandro Mazzola, who spent all 17 years of his senior career at Inter Milan, has died at the age of 83, the club said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Italy forward Sandro Mazzola, who spent all 17 years of his senior career at Inter Milan, has died at the age of 83, the club said on Saturday. Mazzola, considered a club icon at Inter, scored 158 goals in 565 appearances, helping them win four Serie A titles and two European Cups. He was part of the Italy side that won the Euros in 1968 and reached the World Cup final in Mexico two years later. "Sandro Mazzola was one of the greatest footballers in history. Not only in the history of the Nerazzurri," Inter said in a statement on their official website, using a nickname for the team. "He was Inter’s history: he joined the club as a boy and never left it." Mazzola was 6 years old when his father Valentino, also an Italy international, died in the Superga air disaster, a plane crash in May 1949 that killed the entire Torino team on their way back from a match in Lisbon. At 18, Mazzola made his senior debut when Inter fielded their youth side in a match against Juventus, after the Italian federation overturned a decision awarding Inter a 2-0 victory following a pitch invasion by Juventus fans and ordered a replay. Mazzola, who had been a club mascot at Inter as a child, finished a school exam before travelling to Turin, where he scored Inter's only goal from a penalty in a 9-1 defeat to Juventus. He quickly became a first-team regular, helping Inter win their first European Cup in 1964 by scoring a brace as they beat Real Madrid 3-1 in the final. He played a key role when Inter won the title again the next season. Mazzola retired as a player in 1977 and later served as Inter's sporting director. He also became the sporting director of Torino, his father's club. "The star with the moustache shone on the pitch, and still does today. As he often said, he had one final wish: to be remembered as a good man, someone who keeps fighting even when winning is impossible, like in that 9-1," Inter said.

item.title: Braves clinch playoff berth against Astros as Tyler Mahle stars
item.description: Michael Harris II, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson slugged two-run home runs, and deadline acquisition Tyler Mahle continued his exceptional pitching for the visiting Atlanta Braves, who secured a postseason berth with a 6-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Harris II, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson slugged two-run home runs, and deadline acquisition Tyler Mahle continued his exceptional pitching for the visiting Atlanta Braves, who secured a postseason berth with a 6-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Friday. The Braves (90-64) lowered their magic number to clinch the National League East to three over the Philadelphia Phillies, who suffered a 6-3 road loss to the New York Mets earlier on Friday. The Braves have qualified for the postseason eight times over the last nine seasons. Harris provided Mahle a 2-0 lead when he followed a one-out single by Matt Olson with an opposite-field blast to left off Astros starter Peter Lambert (8-10) in the top of the fourth inning. Harris (3-for-5) drove a first-pitch slurve from Lambert 367 feet for his 26th homer of the year. Lambert retired the Braves in order in the first and second innings, and stranded baserunners in the third, fourth and fifth. He departed with one out in the sixth after allowing singles to Olson and Harris before loading the bases with a walk to Ozzie Albies. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh relieved Lambert and left the bases loaded, but Lambert extended his winless streak to 12 consecutive starts after allowing two runs, six hits and one walk while striking out six batters. Acuna followed a one-out walk from Drake Baldwin with his 19th home run in the seventh, a 369-foot line drive to left off Blubaugh that extended the lead to 4-1. With one out in the ninth, Olson bashed his 40th homer the opposite way to left off Astros reliever Enyel De Los Santos. Mahle (7-10) improved to 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA over eight starts since his acquisition from the Giants. He allowed one run on three hits and one walk with six strikeouts over six innings. Yordan Alvarez doubled leading off the fourth and scored when Isaac Paredes followed with a single to center. Alvarez finished 1-for-2 with two walks and had just one plate appearance with a runner on base. Paredes followed the second Alvarez walk in the eighth with an RBI single that plated LaMonte Wade Jr. The Astros (77-77) threatened later in the eighth, but Acuna made a spectacular diving catch that retired Jose Altuve and stranded two baserunners. --Field Level Media

item.title: South Korea justice nominee withdraws in Lee's second cabinet setback as polls slide
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's nominee for justice minister withdrew from consideration on Saturday, the second of Lee's cabinet picks to step aside this month as his approval ratings slump.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's nominee for justice minister withdrew from consideration on Saturday, the second of Lee's cabinet picks to step aside this month as his approval ratings slump. Kim Seung-won's exit follows the withdrawal of Yong Hye-in as nominee for gender-equality minister on Sunday, in the latest fallout from Lee's cabinet [USN:L1N44R00D TEXT:"reshuffle"] in late August. Kim, who said he did not want to add any burden to Lee's administration, criticised a conservative lawmaker who had accused him of lobbying regulators over a drug trial and of financial irregularities. Kim has denied the allegations. "I gravely accept that I did not meet the public's expectations, and I will deeply reflect on my shortcomings," Kim told a press conference. A Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put Lee's public approval at 37%, the lowest since he took office in June 2025, a decline pollsters have partly linked to criticism over his personnel appointments. At a press conference on Friday, Lee acknowledged shortcomings in his administration's screening of nominees. "We are currently working to reexamine our personnel system," the president said.

item.title: Indigenous, civil-society groups sue Prabowo over forest fire response
item.description: A group of indigenous and civil-society organisations in Indonesia's West Kalimantan has filed a class-action lawsuit against President Prabowo Subianto and other authorities over their handling of forest fires in the region, its lawyer said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A group of indigenous and civil-society organisations in Indonesia's West Kalimantan has filed a class-action lawsuit against President Prabowo Subianto and other authorities over their handling of forest fires in the region, its lawyer said on Saturday. Below are more details: The case was registered at the Pontianak court in West Kalimantan with the first hearing scheduled for October 7, the court filing shows. "This lawsuit was filed in response to the West Kalimantan public's concerns over the government's negligence and failure to prevent and tackle forest and land fires that recur every year," Glorio Sanen, the plaintiffs' lawyer told Reuters on Saturday. The presidential office did not immediately respond to request for comment. The plaintiffs are West Kalimantan chapter of the Indigenous Peoples Alliance of the Archipelago, West Kalimantan branch of Catholic Youth, Perkumpulan Laman Punyung Indonesia and an individual, Sisilius Rami, the filing shows. Indonesia is battling its most intense [USN:L1N45807M TEXT:"wildfires"] in 11 years and the government has warned that the fires could continue until November this year. In 2016, a lawsuit was [USN:KCN1UI1DA TEXT:"brought"] by seven Indonesian residents against then-President Joko Widodo, his cabinet ministers and local governments over their handling of forest fires in 2015. After initially winning at the district court, the decision on 2016's lawsuit was overturned when the Supreme Court granted the government's petition for judicial review in 2022, according to media reports.

item.title: Davis Cup roundup: Ben Shelton falls, leaves U.S. tied with Czechs
item.description: Ben Shelton, back in action after reaching the U.S. Open final last week, lost his Davis Cup match Friday as the U.S. team split the opening two singles matches with the Czech Republic in Prague during the opening day of second-round qualifying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ben Shelton, back in action after reaching the U.S. Open final last week, lost his Davis Cup match Friday as the U.S. team split the opening two singles matches with the Czech Republic in Prague during the opening day of second-round qualifying. Jiri Lehecka downed Shelton 6-4, 6-4 in 1 hour, 34 minutes, pulling the Czech team even. In the first singles match, the United States' Learner Tien defeated Jakub Mensik 6-2, 6-4. The series will conclude on Saturday with three matches. The doubles match will feature the United States' Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek opposing Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl, with the reverse singles clashes to follow: Mensik vs. Shelton and Lehecka vs. Tien. Davis Cup series are being contested worldwide this weekend to determine the seven teams that will join defending champion Italy in the final stage at Bologna, Italy, from Nov. 24-29. In Quebec City, Canada jumped out to a 2-0 lead over France. Liam Draxl, ranked 205th in the world, upset 32nd-ranked Arthur Rinderknech 6-2, 7-5, before Felix Auger-Aliassime topped Quentin Halys 7-6 (5), 4-6, 6-3. Austria and Belgium split a pair of matches in Vienna. The hosts grabbed a lead when Jurij Rodionov beat Gauthier Onclin 6-4, 6-1, but Zizou Bergs pulled the Belgians level with a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 triumph over Lukas Neumayer. South Korea established a 2-0 advantage over India in Seoul. Soonwoo Kwon rallied past Dhakshineswar Suresh 3-6, 6-3, 6-4, and Hyeon Chung overtook Sumit Nagal 2-6, 6-4, 7-5. --Field Level Media

item.title: Roman Anthony sparks offense as Red Sox stop Rays' streak
item.description: Roman Anthony homered and had three RBIs, Jahmai Jones went deep and the Boston Red Sox cooled off the first-place Tampa Bay Rays with a 4-2 victory on Friday night in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Roman Anthony homered and had three RBIs, Jahmai Jones went deep and the Boston Red Sox cooled off the first-place Tampa Bay Rays with a 4-2 victory on Friday night in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Red Sox (84-70) opened their final road series of the regular season by scoring all of their runs in the first three innings to win for the second consecutive night. Anthony went 2-for-5, while Caleb Durbin was 2-for-3 as the team produced nine hits. Starting pitcher Ranger Suarez (8-4) fought control issues but went 5 2/3 innings in earning the win. He allowed one run on three hits while striking out five and walking five. Junior Caminero doubled, walked twice and drove in a run for Tampa Bay (93-60), but the American League's top club had only five hits, was a brutal 0-for-13 with runners in scoring position and had its six-game winning streak snapped. Starter Ian Seymour (9-7) was hit hard in the first two innings and finished by allowing four runs on seven hits in five frames. He whiffed five and walked two. On the third pitch of the game, leadoff hitter Anthony crushed a Statcast-estimated 438-foot blast to center field. It was the left fielder's fifth homer. Caminero's RBI groundout tied it in the bottom half, but Anthony did more damage by ripping a two-out single to right for a 3-1 lead in the second. Jones made it 4-1 leading off the third by lining Seymour's changeup out to left for his sixth homer. Suarez got out of a slight jam in the third after Caminero walked and Ryan Vilade singled, but he retired red-hot Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca to maintain the three-run lead. The home club put together a strong threat in the sixth after Wyatt Olds relieved Suarez and issued two walks to fill the bases with two outs. However, he battled back in the count against pinch hitter Jake Fraley and struck him out. In the ninth, Jonathan Aranda's groundout scored a run, but Erik Miller got Simpson to ground out to second with the bases loaded for his fifth save. --Field Level Media

item.title: US clears way for $2.7 billion sale to Ukraine of air-defense development upgrades
item.description: The US State Department approved a potential $2.7 billion military sale to Ukraine for air defense development upgrades and related equipment and services, the department said in a congressional notification late on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The US State Department approved a potential $2.7 billion military sale to Ukraine for air defense development upgrades and related equipment and services, the department said in a congressional notification late on Friday. If the purchase is concluded, Ukraine would finance it using a combination of European contributions and US Foreign Military Financing (FMF) appropriated during the administration of former President Joe Biden , the State Department said in the notification. FMF provides grant assistance that enables countries to purchase weapons and defense equipment produced in the United States. "The FMF will be counted as a US capital contribution to the Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund via a 1:1 reimbursement," the State Department said. The US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund was established as part of a minerals deal signed between the US and Ukraine last year. The package includes S-300 clone missiles, GAM-67 missiles, range-extended air defense laser-guided rocket missile systems, launcher and mobile launching system modification kits and counter-drone system radars, among other weapons systems, the State Department said. The proposed sale is still subject to congressional review. President Donald Trump had said he would end Russia's war in Ukraine when he took office early last year but the goal remains elusive 20 months into his presidency. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. Earlier on Friday, Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill into law, paving the way for increased economic pressure on Russia. Earlier this month, Trump said he would ask European nations to pay back the United States for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine.

item.title: Juan Soto, Mets stop 5-game slide with win over Phillies
item.description: Zac Thornton tossed six solid innings, Juan Soto homered among his three hits and the host New York Mets beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-3 in the second game of a four-game series Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Zac Thornton tossed six solid innings, Juan Soto homered among his three hits and the host New York Mets beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-3 in the second game of a four-game series Friday. Carson Benge laced an RBI single in the first inning to give the Mets (70-84) a lead they'd never relinquish. Fellow rookie outfielder A.J. Ewing added a two-run single two batters later, and Soto delivered a three-run homer in the sixth as New York snapped a five-game losing streak -- its longest since a seven-game slide from June 20-26. Soto was 3-for-5 and Benge and Francisco Lindor finished with two hits for the Mets, who received one hit apiece from their other six starters. Thornton (5-5) gave up two runs on five hits and one walk while striking out four over six innings. He is 5-4 with a 3.26 ERA in 12 starts since his most recent promotion from Triple-A Syracuse. Bryson Stott delivered a run-scoring double in the second before Edmundo Sosa and Derek Hill hit solo homers in the sixth and seventh for the Phillies, who missed a chance to snap a tie with the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League. The Cubs suffered a 6-4 loss to the Cincinnati Reds. Sosa finished 3-for-3 as Philadelphia fell to 7-9 this month. Nate Lavender surrendered Hill's homer in 1 2/3 innings before Dedniel Nunez recorded his first save by tossing 1 1/3 perfect innings. Tim Mayza (3-4), serving in an opener role, took the loss for the Phillies after allowing three runs on three hits and one walk in one-third of an inning. Mayza tossed 32 pitches and had back-to-back 10-pitch battles with Soto and Bo Bichette, the second and third batters he faced. Jose Urquidy relieved Mayza and allowed five hits over 4 2/3 scoreless innings. Urquidy, who was claimed off waivers from the Chicago White Sox on Thursday, walked none while striking out six. --Field Level Media

item.title: LSU QB Sam Leavitt off availability report for Ole Miss showdown
item.description: The Sam Leavitt injury saga took another turn Friday night when the LSU quarterback was removed from the Southeastern Conference's availability report -- just two days after he was deemed doubtful to play.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Sam Leavitt injury saga took another turn Friday night when the LSU quarterback was removed from the Southeastern Conference's availability report -- just two days after he was deemed doubtful to play. LSU upgraded Leavitt from doubtful to questionable Thursday and then took him off the report entirely Friday in time for the No. 7 Tigers' rivalry showdown Saturday against No. 8 Ole Miss in Oxford, Miss. Per the SEC's availability policy, a player designated as doubtful has a 25% chance to play and is "unlikely to play due to significant concerns," while questionable is meant to describe a 50% chance of playing. The nature of Leavitt's injury or when it occurred remains a mystery, with conflicting reports emerging that he had either back spasms or a sore throwing shoulder. ESPN reported Friday that Ole Miss staff do not feel LSU was "sincere" in choosing to list Leavitt -- indicating it could be gamesmanship from Tigers coach Lane Kiffin before he goes up against his most recent program. Kiffin and the Tigers could be in hot water with the league if they were found to be fibbing about Leavitt's health. The SEC policy for football states that the penalty for the first offense regarding an inaccurate or late report is $25,000. It is at the discretion of SEC commissioner Greg Sankey whether to impose a penalty. At a Monday news conference, LSU coach Lane Kiffin did not say anything about Leavitt's health. He also didn't speak on the matter during his weekly radio show on Thursday night. In two games with LSU, Leavitt has completed 41 of 66 passes for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions. The Arizona State transfer has also rushed for 135 yards and five scores. --Field Level Media

item.title: Spencer Horwitz, Konnor Griffin power Pirates past Royals
item.description: Konnor Griffin had four hits and two RBIs, and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh as the Pittsburgh Pirates rallied to win 8-5 over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Konnor Griffin had four hits and two RBIs, and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh as the Pittsburgh Pirates rallied to win 8-5 over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Friday night. Pittsburgh (77-77) trailed 4-0 after the top of the third inning and 5-2 entering the bottom of the fourth but fought back to take the lead in the seventh. With the scored tied 5-5 and Kansas City's Nate Pearson (2-2) pitching, Oneil Cruz reached on an infield single and Nick Gonzales was hit by a pitch. Both advanced on a wild pitch and eventually scored on Horwitz's second hit of the night. Griffin added an RBI single later in the frame, helping the Pirates win their second straight after losing four of their last five. Vinnie Pasquantino and Michael Massey each homered as Kansas City (67-87) scored five runs against Pittsburgh ace Paul Skenes, who scattered six hits and struck out seven in his six innings. After Skenes' exit, the Royals managed just two total hits against relievers Brandon Eisert, Yohan Ramirez (7-4) and Gregory Soto to fall to 5-12 since Aug. 30. Kansas City wasted no time getting to Skenes as Pasquantino lined a two-out solo homer over the right field wall in the first inning. Then with two outs in the third, Pasquantino lined a run-scoring single to right and Maikel Garcia followed with a two-run double. The Pirates got to Royals starter Randy Dobnak in the bottom of the third. After Griffin singled, Brandon Lowe went deep over the right-center-field wall to make it 4-2. Kansas City got a run back in the fourth when Massey turned on a Skenes pitch that landed in the right field seats. Pittsburgh answered in the bottom of that frame with Henry Davis' RBI double to right and Griffin's run-scoring groundout. Dobnak allowed four runs on seven hits and two walks over 3 2/3 innings. Pittsburgh tied it in the fifth when Cruz doubled, went to third on Gonzales' single and scored on a fielder's choice off the bat of Ryan O'Hearn. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eugenio Suarez, Jose Trevino fuel Reds’ comeback win over Cubs
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds scored three times in the sixth inning in a back-and-forth 6-4 win over the visiting Chicago Cubs on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Cincinnati Reds scored three times in the sixth inning in a back-and-forth 6-4 win over the visiting Chicago Cubs on Friday. Starting pitcher Chase Burns allowed two runs on four hits and struck out four in three innings for the Reds (72-82). Cubs starter Clay Holmes (6-8) surrendered six runs on three hits, fanning four while walking five, in 5 1/3 innings. Down by one entering its half of the sixth, Cincinnati went ahead 6-4. Elly De La Cruz drew a leadoff walk and reached third when Holmes' pickoff attempt missed first baseman Michael Busch. Holmes walked Tyler Stephenson and JJ Bleday in consecutive plate appearances, loading the bases. That ended Holmes' outing, and Javier Assad replaced him. Eugenio Suarez singled to left field to score De La Cruz and tie it 4-4. Jose Trevino later drove in Bleday and Suarez with a single that put the hosts up by two. The Reds opened the scoring in the bottom of the first inning. Carlos Jorge tripled to center field to open the frame, and De La Cruz walked. With Sal Stewart at the plate, De La Cruz stole second, and then Jorge scored on Stewart's sacrifice fly that saw De La Cruz tag up and go to third. Stephenson drove in De La Cruz with a single up the middle that hopped off the glove of second baseman Nico Hoerner into center field to make it 2-0. The Cubs (85-69) cut it to 2-1 in the top of the second. Hoerner and Michael Conforto each singled to the outfield, with Hoerner advancing to third on Conforto's hit. Carson Kelly brought Hoerner home with another single. Ian Happ tied it 2-2 in the third with a two-out home run to right-center. Cincinnati went ahead 3-2 in the bottom half. Jorge walked, advanced to third on a De La Cruz single, and scored when Stewart grounded into a double play. Chicago took its first lead in the fourth against reliever Julian Aguiar (1-0). Kelly walked, went to second when Dansby Swanson reached on a forceout. Each advanced on Pete Crow-Armstrong's flyout to center and scored on Seiya Suzuki's single for a 4-3 advantage. --Field Level Media

item.title: Flights resume at Luxembourg Airport after temporary shutdown over drone activity
item.description: Authorities resumed flight operations at Luxembourg Airport on Saturday after suspending services the previous evening following the detection of "unauthorized unmanned aircraft systems", or drones, near and over the aerodrome.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Authorities resumed flight operations at Luxembourg Airport on Saturday after suspending services the previous evening following the detection of "unauthorized unmanned aircraft systems", or drones, near and over the aerodrome. The airport, Luxembourg's sole international airport, said it imposed the suspension on Friday as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of passengers, airline crews, airport personnel and aircraft. The airport did not provide details on the origin of the drones or say who was operating them. While flights have resumed, some delays and disruptions could persist as airlines and airport partners work to restore normal schedules, the airport said in a notice. Luxembourg Airport, the main hub for the country's flag carrier Luxair, said it was continuing to monitor the situation in coordination with relevant authorities.

item.title: Beaches on Australia's west coast to remain shut after fatal shark attack
item.description: Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday, authorities said, after a fatal shark attack at a popular beach in the city on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday, authorities said, after a fatal shark attack at a popular beach in the city on Friday. The victim, a male swimmer, died after being [USN:L1N45A09Q TEXT:"mauled"] at Sorrento Beach, around 20 km (12 miles) from Perth's central business district, prompting the closure of beaches along 17 km (11 miles) of coastline. Beaches in Perth's Joondalup area would remain closed until at least noon (0400 GMT) on Sunday, the state government said on Saturday. "Officers from Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development will continue to conduct land-based patrols," it said in an alert. Friday's incident is the latest in a series of shark attacks in Australia and comes after a surfer in the state was bitten in an attack on Monday. In that attack in the town of Geraldton around 400 km (250 miles) north of Perth, the surfer lost his foot and suffered serious leg injuries, local media said. In June a 35-year-old man was killed while spearfishing off the state's south coast, while a 38-year-old man was mauled to death off an island near Perth in May.

item.title: Poutine accuse l'Ukraine d'ingérence dans les élections législatives russes
item.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré vendredi que l'Ukraine entravait délibérément les négociations visant à mettre fin à la guerre et a accusé Kyiv de s'ingérer dans les élections législatives russes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré vendredi que l'Ukraine entravait délibérément les négociations visant à mettre fin à la guerre et a accusé Kyiv de s'ingérer dans les élections législatives russes. Vladimir Poutine a également réaffirmé devant la commission militaro-industrielle que le principal objectif de Moscou en matière de défense était de s'appuyer sur sa "triade nucléaire" et a déclaré que la Russie devait également s'attacher à améliorer ses défenses antimissiles. Le chef du Kremlin a déclaré que les frappes ukrainiennes sur des cibles russes montraient que les propositions de Kyiv visant à mener des négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre étaient de mauvaise foi. Vladimir Poutine a déclaré qu'une frappe ukrainienne avait récemment touché une maison dans un village situé dans une zone de Zaporijjia occupée par la Russie, tuant le président de la commission électorale locale. "En commettant ce genre de crimes, ils font tout pour s'assurer qu'il n'y ait ni paix ni négociations", a-t-il estimé, selon des propos rapportés par les agences de presse russes. Vladimir Poutine a déclaré que l'Ukraine avait "depuis longtemps sombré dans la dictature", faisant référence au fait que le pays n'avait pas organisé de nouvelle élection présidentielle malgré l'expiration du mandat du président Volodimir Zelensky. "Comme vous le savez, les dirigeants ukrainiens ne sont pas pressés d'organiser des élections, mais ils tentent également de s'ingérer dans nos affaires", a déclaré le président russe. Volodimir Zelensky et d'autres responsables ukrainiens affirment qu'aucune élection ne peut avoir lieu dans leur pays tant que l'état d'urgence, déclaré au début de l'invasion russe de février 2022, reste en vigueur. Kyiv qualifie les élections législatives russes de "pseudo-élections" dont le résultat ne fait aucun doute.
